messages:
Olivia Park: Hey team — after rotating our Redwood key yesterday our Cloud Run service started getting 401 invalid_api_key on every request. No code changes except the secret rotation. Example curl from the container (sanitized):

```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer \"$REDWOOD_API_KEY\"' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

Response body: {\"error\":{\"type\":\"invalid_api_key\",\"message\":\"Invalid API key provided\"}}

Any clues? We pulled the secret from Google Secret Manager using the runtime library — maybe something odd with the value?

Priya Nair: thanks for the report, Olivia. Can you paste the full Authorization header as your service sends it (mask most of the key, last 6 chars are fine)? Also what runtime/language?

Olivia Park: running node14 on Cloud Run. Here's the header captured in our app logs (we log headers masked):
Authorization: Bearer \"sk_live_3jf4...9x7Y\"

Evan Chen: Aha — I think the key in Secret Manager includes extra quotes. Some SDKs return the raw secret payload including surrounding quotes if the secret was stored as a JSON/string literal. If the header contains quotes it won't match server side. Can you run: `echo \"$REDWOOD_API_KEY\" | hexdump -C` inside the container to check for leading/trailing quote (0x22) or newline (0x0a)?

Olivia Park: ran the hexdump, output shows the first byte is 22 and the last visible byte is 22 before the newline:
00000000  22 73 6b 5f 6c 69 76 65  5f 33 6a 66 34 2e 2e 2e  |\"sk_live_3jf4...|
00000010  39 78 37 59 22 0a                                    |9x7Y\".|

Marta Lopez: yep that's the culprit — the secret was stored with quotes, likely when someone pasted a JSON-encoded value into Secret Manager. Redwood expects the raw key bytes (no surrounding quotes). When your app sets header Authorization: Bearer \"sk_live_...\" the backend treats the extra quote characters as part of the token and rejects it (401 invalid_api_key).

Priya Nair: Quick remediation: update the secret to the unquoted string or strip quotes at read-time. Example fixes: (1) Fix secret value via console/CLI to remove the quotes. (2) Workaround in runtime: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret=REDWOOD_API_KEY | tr -d '"' | tr -d '\n')` or in Node: `const key = (await sm.getSecret()).replace(/^"|"$/g, '').trim()`

Olivia Park: removing quotes from Secret Manager fixed it — calls are succeeding again. Thanks! Any chance we can detect and give a clearer error for this on your side? 401 just says invalid_api_key which didn't hint at extra chars.

Evan Chen: Good point. I'll file an internal engineering ticket to add a diagnostic to logs for malformed-token characters (non-alphanumeric safe chars) while preserving security (only log token shape/hex bytes, never full key). That should help support triage for cases like this.

support-bot: Ticket created: INF-2147 — detect/troubleshoot quoted or padded API keys in auth header (assigned to eng-runtime).

Marta Lopez: Also adding a note to the onboarding docs and the Secret Manager guide: "If copying secrets from JSON blobs, ensure you store the raw key string without surrounding quotes or newlines." I'll link the doc update in the ticket.

Olivia Park: Appreciate the quick help — leaving the thread in case anyone else hits the same thing. :thumbsup:

Priya Nair: marking resolved on our side. If it reappears please include a masked header and hexdump output.
